title: How a screen feels your finger

probes.question: Why does a finger register on a capacitive screen?
options: The body is a conductor and distorts the screen's electrostatic field
It blocks a beam of light

probes.question: A touch is measured as a change in ____.

image.alt: A phone touchscreen showing the faint diamond-shaped grid of conductive tracks across its surface.

panels.text: A capacitive touchscreen is glass coated with a transparent conductor, such as indium tin oxide.
The coating sets up an electrostatic field across the screen.
Your body is an electrical conductor too. When you touch the glass, the field is distorted, and the change in capacitance can be measured.
The twist: the first finger-driven touchscreen was developed by Eric Johnson at the Royal Radar Establishment in Malvern, England, and described in 1965.
